errors.checklistItem: the Buttonhole Direction dominates the frame, identifiable within one second, framed macro on the buttonhole
errors.expected: Macro crop on two or three adjacent placket buttonholes.
errors.actual: Three buttonholes are in frame; the centre one is complete, while the top and bottom buttonholes are clipped by the frame edges. Inherent to a tight macro crop and does not obscure the showcased feature - the fully-visible centre buttonhole reads unambiguously.
errors.correction: Acceptable as delivered; no action required.

lockedFeatures: vertical buttonhole orientation - CORRECT: every buttonhole is a vertical slit running exactly parallel to the placket edges, ~0 deg deviation from the placket axis. Measured on the centre buttonhole: slit runs from y=530 to y=700 at x=432 in an 880x1168 frame, i.e. clearly taller than wide. Instantly readable as vertical at thumbnail scale.

thread and bar tack - CORRECT: dense white machine buttonhole stitching down BOTH long sides of each slit, with a bar tack at BOTH the top terminus and the bottom terminus, exactly as notated in the drawing.
keyhole vs straight - CORRECT: straight (non-keyhole) buttonhole; no teardrop/eyelet enlargement at either end, matching the drawing.
buttonhole stitch - CORRECT: machine-worked purl-edge buttonhole in fine white thread, matching the drawing's stitch notation; no hand/Milanese substitution.
eyelet holes - PRESENT: 4-hole pearlised buttons, all four holes clearly rendered with a cross-stitch shank.
orientation front - CORRECT: front face of the garment, front placket and button stance toward the viewer; no back or side feature present.
placket construction - CORRECT: applied front placket band topstitched along BOTH long edges (topstitch lines at x=363 and x=494), matching the drawing's double dashed topstitch notation.
button placement - CORRECT: buttons on the placket centreline. Placket spans x=363-494 (centre 428.5); button centre x=432, a 2.7% deviation, within the <2-3% blueprint tolerance.
no sibling substitution - CONFIRMED: zero horizontal buttonholes anywhere in frame; not bh-vertical-horiz, not bh-horiz-2nd, not a concealed/hidden placket.

no annotation - CONFIRMED: full frame contrast-stretched (linear 3x, -300 offset) to hunt for faint marks; no text, numbers, units, arrows, leader or dimension lines, ruler ticks, callouts, labels or watermark anywhere.

no competing subject - CONFIRMED: no head, face, chin, beard, neck, bare skin, collar, cuff or shoulder in frame; no location, architecture, furniture, scenery or props. Pressed white cotton and the buttoned placket only, with natural worn drape and soft directional studio light.
notes: Attempt 2, after attempt 1 was rejected purely on framing (major composition error: 8.6% feature dominance, 25px buttonholes needing 5x magnification to read, plus the model's chin/beard/neck in frame). The correction was applied by appending a COMPOSITION OVERRIDE macro-crop block; all locked geometry/construction blocks were left untouched, and the blueprint was re-attached as the geometry reference on the retry (reference_images confirmed in the job payload). Result: buttonhole scale increased roughly 5x (centre buttonhole now ~170px of a 1168px frame, ~15% of frame height) and the vertical orientation is now identifiable in well under one second; all competing elements are gone. Adversarial verification performed at 4x zoom on two separate buttonholes plus a contrast-stretched full-frame text/watermark scan. The blueprint/text consistency gate had already passed pre-generation: the drawing (full front technical flat, point collar, 1 neck button + 6 placket buttons) shows every buttonhole as a vertical slit with top and bottom bar tacks, and the lower placket was inspected specifically to rule out a horizontal buttonhole - none present - which agrees with label 'Vertical' and description 'Standard vertical buttonholes - formal preferred.' No discrepancy found against the drawing on any of the nine categories.
